solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chap in great trouble having to catch European bird

indicators.note: the chap is placed in the middle of the trouble, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taking great trouble over something is taking pains
Ted is a man's name, standing for any chap
to nip is to catch or pinch

explanation.surface: A man in serious difficulty has to grab a bird from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: PAINS is the plural noun of 'take great pains'; the bird is a wader of Africa and Asia, not Europe, which makes 'European' look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The painted snipe is a wading species with striking plumage, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Critical speech revealed by microphone below boom?

indicators.note: in a down entry the microphone piece comes below, that is after, the boom piece

parts.note: a boom is a long pole, such as the one a sound recordist holds
mic is the short form of microphone

explanation.surface: A harsh speech is picked up by a mic dangling from a boom, as on a film set.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemic is a strongly worded attack on someone's views, a critical speech or piece of writing.

clue.text: Levy on departures, hence taxi and train are badly used

indicators.note: letters that are badly used are misapplied and jumbled, so the words hence taxi and train are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a fare tax makes taxis and trains badly used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departures' looks like travel, matching taxi and train, but here it means deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Death duty is charged on an estate when someone dies; departures is a euphemism for deaths.

clue.text: Number of runs acquired by the English

indicators.note: the runs piece is taken in by, so held inside, the words for the English

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket score: how many runs the English side got.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a small whole number, a plain example of a number.

clue.text: Throw away fish savoury item

parts.note: to dump something is to throw it away
ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Discard the fish dish you have been served.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumpling is a small savoury ball of dough cooked in stew or soup.

clue.text: Standard choice of starters on naff menu

indicators.note: the choice word is set among the starting letters, so it is enclosed by them
starters are the opening letters, here of naff and menu

parts.note: or is the word that offers a choice between alternatives

explanation.surface: The usual selection of first courses on an uninspiring restaurant menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' looks like the menu's first courses but means the first letters N and M; 'naff' is British slang for tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the usual or accepted standard against which things are measured.

clue.text: French lake — it has fish taken all over for scientific examination

indicators.note: the whole string is taken over, turned end to end, so it is read backwards

parts.note: lac is the French word for lake
the carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A French lake and its fish being studied all over in a scientific survey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken all over' reverses the whole of LAC IT CARP.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a practical is a hands-on laboratory test in a science subject.

clue.text: Where the Pope may be wrong as to Golden Calf?

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters are put wrongly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the Pope off course in a matter of the Golden Calf, the idol of the Old Testament?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where the Pope may be' reads like 'where he may be wrong', but it is the definition: a place he visits.
explanation.definitionFit: Castel Gandolfo near Rome is the Pope's traditional summer residence, so a place he may be found.

clue.text: Rubbish cut by editor — he's beginning to be very good

indicators.note: the rubbish word is cut into by the other pieces, which go inside it

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the word he's

explanation.surface: An editor slashing junk copy is starting to be very good at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-hot is informal for extremely skilled or excellent, so very good.

clue.text: Hard cutting tragic role for operetta composer

indicators.note: the hard piece cuts into the role name, so it goes inside it

parts.note: King Lear is the title role of Shakespeare's tragedy
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A difficult edit to a tragic part for a writer of light opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian composer of The Merry Widow, a famous operetta.

clue.text: Mother alarmed when shunted about in jam

parts.note: ma is a familiar name for mother

indicators.note: shunted about means moved around, so the letters of alarmed are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mum got alarmed when her train was shunted around and stuck in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' looks like a traffic jam to go with 'shunted', but it is the preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus preserve, a kind of jam in the broad sense.

clue.text: Damage to include a length of old coastal defence

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: the word to includes the length piece, holding it inside

parts.note: the ell is an old unit of length, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: Harm comes to an old sea defence over some length of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Martello towers are small round forts built along British coasts against Napoleonic invasion.

clue.text: Sadist's outside with strong desire for pain

indicators.note: outside picks the letters at the outer edges of the word Sadist

parts.note: an itch is a restless, strong desire for something

explanation.surface: A sadist on the outside harbours a keen craving for pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sudden sharp pain in the side, often from running.

clue.text: Hearing sound of bell on puss

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: puss is a pet name for a cat
ching is an imitative word for a ringing bell

explanation.surface: Hearing the tinkle of a bell on the cat's collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' seems to go with the bell's sound but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching a remark means managing to hear it, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Hymn referred to as old, end-of-the-century?

definitions.meaning: the traditional tune for All People That On Earth Do Dwell
a century has a hundred items, so its last one comes in that position

explanation.surface: An old hymn sung to mark the close of a century.
explanation.walkthrough: A century is any hundred, so its end is the item numbered 100; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal for 100 names the final place in a set of a hundred, and the Old Hundredth names the hymn tune.

clue.text: Make figures half responsible for blocking street

indicators.note: the shortened word blocks the street, sitting inside its abbreviation
only half of the synonym for responsible is kept, its first four letters

parts.note: culpable means responsible for wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Someone partly to blame for blocking a road is told to make figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To sculpt is to carve or model statues, making figures from stone or clay.

clue.text: Am lifting well-boring plant, ancient garden annual

indicators.note: in a down entry lifting sends the word upward, so it reads in reverse

parts.note: a rig is the plant or apparatus used to drill wells
old means ancient

explanation.surface: I'm hoisting a drilling rig, an ancient yearly garden show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like the definition but means industrial equipment; the annual is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The pot marigold is a bright orange flower usually grown as an annual in gardens.

clue.text: First light never begins for blind

indicators.note: the word never starts, so its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: dawning is daybreak, the first light of morning

explanation.surface: Daybreak never comes for someone who cannot see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blind' looks like an adjective for a sightless person but is a noun, a shade.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas sheet over a window or shopfront, a kind of sunshade or blind.

clue.text: Appoint a second operator, perhaps

parts.note: a mathematical operator such as plus or minus is written as a sign

explanation.surface: Take on a second switchboard operator.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign someone is to appoint them to a post or task.

clue.text: Son gets on with everything except gym kit

indicators.note: in an across entry the son piece gets on the end, after the others

parts.note: all means everything
bar means except, as in all bar one
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy gets along with everything apart from the gym equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall bars are rungs fixed to a gymnasium wall for exercises, standard gym equipment.

clue.text: Unproductive anger follows set going wrong

indicators.note: the anger piece follows, so it comes after the jumbled letters
going wrong means the letters go astray and are rearranged

parts.note: to rile is to anger or annoy

explanation.surface: Fruitless fury follows when a film set goes awry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile land or effort yields nothing, so it is barren and unproductive.

clue.text: Do wrong breaking into reserved wine

indicators.note: the wrongdoing piece breaks into the other, landing inside it

parts.note: shy means reserved or retiring
to err is to do wrong

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaves by breaking into a bottle kept for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserved' suggests a wine set aside, but it means timid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from southern Spain.

clue.text: Reckon wrongly and nearly omit to come to a conclusion

indicators.note: nearly drops the last letter, leaving almost the whole word

parts.note: to miss something out is to omit it
to judge is to form an opinion or reach a conclusion

explanation.surface: Getting a reckoning wrong, nearly skipping a step before deciding.
explanation.definitionFit: To misjudge is to form a wrong estimate or opinion of something.

clue.text: Card game Jack's leading — no pressure

indicators.note: the jack piece leads, going in front of the rest

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: no pressure means the pressure letter is removed

parts.note: poker is a card game
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: In a card game the jack is led, with no pressure on the player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card game' reads as one phrase, but 'Card' is the definition and 'game' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The joker is an extra playing card with a jester picture, often used as a wild card.

clue.text: Bento full — with this in it?

definitions.text: Bento full — with this in it?

indicators.note: the answer is literally in the words Bento full, spanning the two

explanation.surface: A packed Japanese lunch box: what might fill it?
explanation.walkthrough: A bento is a Japanese boxed lunch, which may well contain this bean curd.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu, or bean curd, is a staple Japanese ingredient often packed in a bento lunch.

clue.text: Giordano's composed in a rather overblown style

indicators.note: composed means put together in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Umberto Giordano, the Italian opera composer, wrote in a somewhat pompous manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandioso is an Italian musical direction meaning in a grand, imposing style.

clue.text: Excellent price reported for imported ice cream

indicators.note: reported signals that the words are heard, so we go by their sound

parts.note: cool means excellent and a fee is a price, together cool fee

explanation.surface: A great price is quoted for an ice cream brought in from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Kulfi is a dense frozen dairy dessert from South Asia, so an ice cream imported to Britain.

clue.text: Ought the Queen note somebody on which her sword rests?

parts.note: should means ought, as in you should go
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher
B is a note of the musical scale
one means somebody, as in one never knows

explanation.surface: Should Her Majesty pick out somebody to knight?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition pictures the Queen dubbing a knight, laying the sword on the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: At a dubbing ceremony the monarch's blade touches each shoulder, so this bone is where it rests.
